newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end down, trade cautious.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end down, trade cautious.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares closed lower on Wednesday in cautious trade, though analysts said the outlook for the days ahead was mildly positive.
The B share index lost 1.99 points, or 1.17 percent, to close at 167.66. Turnover was HK$109.7 million compared with Tuesday's HK$216.7 million.
The A share index gained 3.03 points, or 0.71 percent, to 428.77 on turnover of 10.3 billion yuan, compared with 12.4 billion yuan on Tuesday.

"Investors are wavering between bargain-hunting and profit-taking given no real news to drive the index up or down," a trader at J&A Securities said. "And more buying is expected tomorrow after today's losses."
"The general trend is good, but investors are reluctant to buy stakes with high risks during the company reporting season," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The deadline for listed companies to post their 1996 results is April 30, but only one of the 43 B share companies listed in Shenzhen has made their 1996 results public.

Analysts and traders said a new provision on securities crimes, which was added for the first time to the criminal law to help check insider trading and price manipulation, did not dampen market sentiment.
The law was revised last week by the National People's Congress, or parliament, and will come into effect on October 1, official media have said.
On the B share market, beverage maker Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co Ltd was the biggest loser, dropping HK$0.24 or 3.84 percent ro HK$6.01.
On the A share market, the best performer was television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd which gained 1.62 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up of 17.79 yuan on volume of 55.2 million shares.
